record.question: What ruler can detect controller-subordinate interaction?
record.what_happened: A ruler for controller-subordinate interaction: defer. Licensed by H06, H07, H10, H15, H03; the transfer gap is V13 records who corrected whom; a text or log corpus needs correction events with actors. Without them the ruler has no input and only the artifact-floor result.
record.what_changed_in_the_project_world: A text-side design is exported with its gap, its records, its baseline and its failure meaning attached; nothing here is human evidence.
record.what_remains_a_rival: if coherence separates the teams, the corpus leaked the director into the artifact

hypothesis: H06, H07, H10 and H15 become a crossed-role, hidden-intervention protocol with coherence and style as rivals.

H06.what_happened: Suppression and amplification routes were classified 100% and 75% of the time and the next intervention was predicted at a log score of -0.48 against -0.69 for a coin flip.

H07.what_happened: Across two directors and two domains, the correction route followed the subordinate's style in at least 84% of teams in every cell.

H10.what_happened: A model of how the controller handled each mistake predicted whether a revision followed +0.57 nats better than the revision frequency; corrected was revised 100%, accepted was revised 0%, exploited was revised 0%, concealed was revised 100%, missed was revised 0%.

H15.what_happened: The graph model predicted the hidden next intervention at a log score of -1.08 against -0.98 for the best baseline.

H03.what_happened: Director versus shared brief: artifact-only 50%, coherence 50%, interaction records 100% against 50% chance.

deliverable.title: A ruler for controller-subordinate interaction

protocol.crossed_roles: the same subordinates under different controllers and domains; attribution must follow the correction relation (H07)
protocol.hidden_intervention: hide the next correction; a graph model must beat role frequency, coherence, identity and token share (H15)
protocol.signatures: suppression versus amplification from proposal-to-realization change (H06)

deliverable.transfer_gap: V13 records who corrected whom; a text or log corpus needs correction events with actors. Without them the ruler has no input and only the artifact-floor result (H03) transfers.
deliverable.sounding_line_target: collaboration logs and revision histories with actor-attributed operations (the contribution network's per-actor relations)
deliverable.records_required: proposal, correction and realization events with actor ids; a hidden next intervention to predict
deliverable.positive_gate: a constructed log corpus with paired central and shared-brief teams where the artifact classifier is at floor and the interaction reader is not
deliverable.failure_meaning: if coherence separates the teams, the corpus leaked the director into the artifact
deliverable.human_evidence_boundary: the ruler reads records of operations; it does not attribute authorship or intent to people

gates.name: no_human_claim_in_the_boundary
gates.detail: a task whose answer is known by construction returns that answer

gates_summary.how_to_read: a gate RECORDS here and does not raise, so an exploratory sweep is never killed mid-run. tests/test_gates.py walks every committed verdict and fails the suite on anything in failed_names or unexpected_passes, which puts the hard stop where a result would become public. THREE categories, and they are not the same thing: failed_names is a control that broke; documented_failures is a gate marked expected_to_fail, which records a KNOWN defect so the evidence travels with the result (S-2's dead manipulation, S-3's fitted threshold); unexpected_passes is a documented defect that has started passing, which means somebody fixed it without updating the gate and is the one nobody would otherwise notice. A skipped gate counts as passing but is reported separately: it means an optional dependency was absent, never that a check succeeded.
